keyVerseText: Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun סְגֻלָּה (çᵉgullâh) is derived from a feminine passive participle form of an unused root meaning "to shut up." This etymology suggests the idea of something closely guarded or set apart, emphasizing a sense of treasured possession that is carefully preserved. Beyond the common English gloss of "peculiar treasure" or "jewel," the root sense enriches the meaning by highlighting the exclusivity and protected status of what is valued.
usageInScripture: The word סְגֻלָּה appears eight times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently conveying the idea of valued possession or treasured property. It is used to describe Israel as God's chosen people, a "peculiar treasure," as well as literal treasures such as gold and silver in royal contexts. The range of English translations—"peculiar treasure," "special," "proper good," and "my jewels"—reflects both the metaphorical and material senses, underscoring the word's association with something set apart for special honor and value.
theologicalSignificance: The concept of סְגֻלָּה is profoundly significant for understanding God's relationship with His people. It conveys that Israel is uniquely chosen and treasured by God, not merely as a possession but as a people set apart for His covenant purposes. This treasured status implies responsibility and privilege, reflecting God's sovereign grace in selecting and preserving His people. For the Christian faith, this term prefigures the special calling of believers as God's own possession, called to live in obedience and holiness as a reflection of God's redeeming love.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 19:5 states, "then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people," highlighting the covenantal promise that obedience leads to a unique and valued relationship with God. The word סְגֻלָּה here emphasizes not only the privilege of being chosen but also the exclusivity and preciousness of Israel to God. This treasured status is grounded in God's sovereign ownership of the earth, underscoring that His people are set apart by His will and purpose.
